title: The ache of missing God
hook: the gopis miss Krishna so much that the wise man sent to teach them learns bhakti from them
carry: missing God is a mark of bhakti
tomorrow: can you find something you never lost?

segments.voice: Yesterday: bhakti, and the opening of the Narada Bhakti Sutras: now, then, we will explain bhakti. The definition is supreme love.

Krishna has left the village of Vraja for the city of Mathura, and he hasn't come back. The cowherd women who loved him, the gopis, can't stop talking about him. So he sends his friend Uddhava, a wise and learned man, with a message: I was never really apart from you; turn your minds inward and you'll find me. Uddhava arrives to comfort them. In the Bhagavata Purana, he ends up being the one who's taught.
screen: `KRISHNA HAS LEFT VRAJA.` → `A WISE MAN SENT TO COMFORT.` → `HE ENDS UP BEING TAUGHT.`

segments.voice: The gopis hear the message, and they weep. One of them talks to a passing bee as if it were Krishna's messenger, half angry, half in love. They don't want a lesson; they want him. And Uddhava, the man of knowledge, is undone. He stays for months, and before he goes he says he'd gladly be a bush or a creeper in Vraja, just to be touched by the dust of those women's feet. Many teachers read it this way: knowledge came to teach love, and love taught knowledge. And a short Sanskrit book, the Narada Bhakti Sutras, points to the gopis as its example. Having defined bhakti as supreme love, it asks: what are its marks? Three teachers answer first. Vyasa: fondness for worship, the lamp and the flowers. Garga: fondness for the stories of the Lord. Shandilya: delight in the Self. Then Narada's own view: bhakti is offering every action to the Lord, and feeling deep anguish on forgetting him. The word is vyakulata: turmoil, the way a parent feels who loses a child in a crowd. Here's the teaching, one of Hinduism's most tender: missing God isn't a failure of devotion. It's one of its marks. Bhakti poets call love in separation viraha, and they've sung it for centuries. The sutras add one guardrail: even the gopis never forgot who Krishna was. So if your puja has slipped, many teachers would say the ache you feel isn't the door closing. It's the door.
screen: `THE GOPIS WEEP; A BEE GETS AN EARFUL.` · `UDDHAVA: LET ME BE A BUSH IN VRAJA.` · `FOUR TEACHERS, FOUR MARKS.` · `NARADA: ANGUISH ON FORGETTING.` · then, large: `MISSING GOD IS A MARK OF BHAKTI.`

segments.voice: If you pray, say one name of God you love, Krishna, Rama, Shiva, Devi, slowly, a few times, the way many Hindus do in japa. Between the names, notice any small ache of distance. Don't fix it; Narada counts it as love. If you don't pray, do the same with the name of someone you miss, and let the missing be what it is: a sign of how much they matter.
Bhakti. Devotion. Vyasa sees it in worship, Garga in the stories, Shandilya in delight, and Narada in the ache of forgetting. The gopis lived all four.
Hold on to this: missing God is a mark of bhakti. The gopis knew it. Day six hundred ninety-four, done.

screen: `DAY 694 COUNTS.` → `TOMORROW: CAN YOU FIND SOMETHING YOU NEVER LOST?`

howItsDone: In many Vaishnava homes and temples, songs of longing for Krishna, often in the gopis' voice, are sung at evening aarti and in kirtan; poets call this love in separation viraha. Devotion also takes the other shapes the sutras name: daily puja, retelling the stories, and offering one's work to God.

fork.setup: your aunt hasn't been to the temple in months. she says she feels far from God and guilty about it. by Narada's sutras, what's true?

fork.reveal: sutra nineteen: offering every act, and deep anguish on forgetting him. the gopis missed Krishna, and the sutras call them the model.

original.note: Sanskrit vyākulatā, turmoil, distress: Narada's mark of bhakti is this anguish on forgetting the Lord.

trapdoor: what you thought: devotion means always feeling close to God.
what it means: for Narada, the ache of forgetting, of distance, is one of bhakti's marks; the gopis missing Krishna are his example.
what a scholar hears: sutras 15–24 cite Parasharya (Vyasa), Garga and Shandilya before Narada's own view; the Bhagavata's Uddhava episode (10.46–47) is the classic picture of viraha.

tie.story: Krishna left Vraja, and the gopis missed him so much that Uddhava, sent to teach them, learned devotion from them instead.
tie.friend: Priya's guilty ache after a week without aarti is, by Narada's measure, a sign of her bhakti and a way back to Nani's lamp.

Vyasa.meaning: the sage tradition credits with the Mahabharata

Garga.meaning: a sage who sees bhakti in love of the stories

Shandilya.meaning: a sage who sees bhakti in delight in the Self

vyakulata.meaning: turmoil, anguish: Narada's mark of bhakti

Vraja.meaning: Krishna's childhood country, also called Braj

gopis.meaning: the cowherd women who loved Krishna

Uddhava.meaning: Krishna's wise friend, sent to comfort the gopis

viraha.meaning: love in separation, longing for the beloved

Bhagavata Purana.meaning: a Purana of Vishnu's stories, including Krishna's
